open_points.subject: same-byte re-upload invalidating an import confirmation
open_points.text: A16 requires that confirming after another upload be refused “also when the new file has the same bytes,” but A13 binds the confirmation to “the file's digest and the picks,” and A16 says it “applies the file of that digest”; M11 carries no upload-instance identity or generation.
open_points.question: How can Registry distinguish the replaced upload from a later upload of identical bytes and therefore decide whether the pending confirmation is still valid?
options: Treat equal bytes and the same digest as the bound file, so the old confirmation remains valid.
Give each upload an additional occurrence identity or generation and bind the confirmation to it, so any later upload invalidates the confirmation even when its bytes are identical.
open_points.default_guess: Track an upload generation in the owner session and bind the confirmation to it.

witness.initial: A valid owner session has uploaded file F, received a clean mapping, and holds confirmation value C bound to F's digest and the selected mapping inputs.
events: The owner uploads F again in the same session with exactly the same bytes.
The owner submits the unchanged mapping with confirmation value C.
outcomes: A16 rule 2 and required test 3 require refusal because the upload that C named was replaced, even though the replacement has the same bytes.
Under A13's stated binding, the current file has the same digest and the inputs still match, so the submission passes the binding and the import may be accepted.
witness.observer: The owner sees refusal versus a committed import; the store and audit log likewise differ.
